notes: The schematic image was not available. I built the standard 2N7000 level shifter, as the text describes: gate to the board's 3.3 V (VCC), source to the 3.3 V data pin, drain to the NeoPixel DIN, and the 10k resistor from the drain to the 5 V rail. The NeoPixel is powered from the 5 V rail.
I added wire7 (GND rail to NeoPixel VSS), which step 1 did not have. The NeoPixel needs a ground return and the count in step 1 was only an estimate.
The catalogue card for arduino-mkr-gsm-1400 has no digital pins. I used 'D6' for the data pin, assuming pin 6, which the tutorial text does not state. The name is not on the card.
I used one single `neopixel` instead of the ring, as the tutorial's breadboard layout does. DOUT is inserted but left unconnected.
The LiPo battery plugs into the board's JST connector, so I modelled it as bat1 '+' joined to mkr1 BAT. The battery's negative terminal is not modelled separately.
The board is powered over USB for programming. The USB cable is not on the parts list, so it is not a node.
Breadboard positions are my own choice, since there was no image. Rails: tp is 5 V and tn is GND.
